name_note: The GTDB species name matches the name used in papers; a few genomes GTDB places here are labelled Clostridium disporicum in NCBI.

sentences.text: Clostridium saudiense is described as a commensal bacterium of the human gut that has recently been included in the Clostridium celatum group.
A case report describes bacteremia and an iliopsoas abscess due to Clostridium saudiense in an 82-year-old woman, confirmed by 16S rDNA gene sequencing.
That report states that infections caused by these bacteria are rarely reported, and its literature review identified six additional cases of Clostridium celatum group infections.
A study of arsenic-exposed populations of West Bengal, India, using amplicon sequencing of stool DNA, reported a significant increase in Clostridium saudiense alongside several other species.
In Egyptian multiple sclerosis patients studied with long-read sequencing of the full 16S rRNA gene, relapsing multiple sclerosis showed increased Clostridium saudiense.
